title: Lease-based cohort handshake rollout with rollback telemetry
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: we need a rollout primitive that guarantees a short-lived stake (lease) for cohorts so that canaries and shadow validations can be deterministically drained if telemetry shows regression. This PR implements a lease-based cohort handshake protocol and ties it into existing rollout controller and telemetry-driven rollback hooks. The implementation goals were: 1) minimize runtime surface area (no new long-lived state machines in the serving runtime), 2) ensure deterministic rollback and replayability for debugging, 3) provide clear observability events for each handshake step so SRE can automate final rollback decisions. Key behavior: - A cohort is issued a time-bound lease when promoted to receive traffic (canary or staged A/B). The lease contains a handshake token and expiry. - Handshake step: client-side router (or the rollout controller) exchanges the token with the serving plane to confirm session affinity and KV-cache priming. - Shadow validation pass: during the lease window, shadow traffic is run against the new model variant and responses are scored by configured metric hooks. - Safety gates: disagreement detector, latency tail guard, and quality-regression threshold are evaluated in a sliding window. Each gate emits an event with deterministic metadata (cohort_id, lease_id, metric_snapshot, trace_id). - Automated rollback: if any gate breaches its configured threshold (or a quorum of gates signals failure), the rollout controller revokes the lease and initiates an immediate drain + replay snapshot for forensics. - Replayability: revoked leases are checkpointed (hash of input batch + model version + seed) so failing requests can be replayed in the debug harness. This PR contains: - rollout controller changes to issue and track leases (controllers/lease_controller.go) - a lightweight handshake module in the router (router/lease_handshake.go) - telemetry hooks to publish lease-scoped events (telemetry/lease_events.v1.proto and telemetry/publishers.go) - CLI to force-revoke a lease and dump checkpointed replays (tools/rw-leasectl) - tests: unit + integration + a small canary-sim harness that runs simulated traffic patterns and asserts deterministic behavior. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2345) - [x] Unit tests for handshake and lease expiry behavior - [x] Integration test for shadow validation pass-through logic - [x] Canary-sim verified regression and rollback scenario - [x] Observability: events and dashboards updated - [x] Manual runbook added for emergency lease revocation Backwards compatibility: the handshake is opt-in per rollout spec (defaults to off). Existing rollouts without leases behave exactly as today. Rollout spec extension: added optional fields `lease.enabled`, `lease.duration_s`, and `lease.quorum` (see docs on rollout API). Security: handshake tokens are HMAC-signed with the server KMS key and have a short TTL. Performance: handshake path is O(1) additional RPC for the first request from a cohort; subsequent requests flow normally with session affinity. See 'rationale' and 'perf notes' below for microbenchmarks. Rationale: prior incidents (SUP-1128) showed noisy shadow validation and long-lived partial promotions made rollback windows fuzzy. Lease semantics provide a clear, time-boxed promotion that makes automated rollback safe and replayable. Perf notes: - Local microbench: handshake added ~350us p50 on first request in a synthetic bench (measured on a T4-equivalent test VM). - KV priming in the handshake saved ~1.8% token cost on long tail workloads by avoiding repeated cold-start tokens in early requests. - End-to-end canary-sim with 10k synthetic requests sustained controller decisions within the SLA (rolling decision latency < 2s).
commits_summary: Initial controller and router handshake scaffold
Add lease event proto and telemetry publisher hooks
Implement CLI tooling for lease inspection and revocation
Add canary-sim integration test and deterministic replay checkpoints
Fix race in controller lease expiry (addressed by exponential backoff loop)
review_comments: Luca Romano: Nice approach — I like the lease semantics. A couple of questions: 1) what prevents churn if a bad network causes premature revocations? 2) can we avoid checkpointing full request bodies for GDPR concerns?

Maya Patel: Reply: we added a backoff + grace period before final revocation to tolerate transient network blips; grace window is configurable. For GDPR we hash and store only non-PII request-derived fingerprints (sha256) and retention is configurable; details in runbook.

Priya Desai: Please add an integration test for a multi-cohort swap where two cohorts are promoted simultaneously (race case). Also request small refactor to make the telemetry publisher non-blocking.
Maya Patel: Added multi-cohort test and switched publisher to background worker with bounded channel; update pushed in commit 4. CI re-run shows flakiness fixed.
Ethan Brooks: Approve after CI green. Left a minor nit on naming lease_id -> lease_token for clarity (not blocking).
CI Bot: Integration tests initially failed (canary_sim) due to deterministic seed mismatch; fixed by normalizing RNG seed in harness. All checks passed after fix.
ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (microbench results attached in artifact)
notes_on_deployment: Feature is gated by rollout spec. Ops rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag, 2) enable for internal staging only for one week, 3) enable for beta customers with telemetry collection, 4) general availability. Dashboards and alert rules added under 'Lease Rollouts'.
release_notes: Introduces lease-based cohort handshake for rollouts: opt-in rollout spec fields, deterministic lease-scoped telemetry, automated lease revocation and checkpointed replay for forensic debugging. Safe-by-default; off unless enabled in rollout spec.
forensics_guidance: Revoked leases produce a checkpoint manifest (lease_id, cohort_id, model_version, input_fingerprint_list). Use tools/rw-leasectl to export replay bundles and run them in the debug harness. Follow runbook to redact PII before sharing with engineering.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental mass revocation due to misconfigured thresholds. Mitigation: default conservative quorum, automatic dry-run mode for first 72h, and an admin approval step for global enable. Also added a safety 'circuit breaker' to pause all lease issuance if controller error rate exceeds 5% for 1m.
qa_notes: Test matrix included: single-cohort canary, multi-cohort simultaneous promotion, network partition (grace window), GDPR retention compliance, and replay fidelity. Canary-sim artifacts uploaded to CI artifact store.
related_work: References: ENG-2345 design doc, SUP-1128 incident notes. Inspired by bounded leases used in database leader elections but adapted for short-lived rollout promotions.
postmerge_actions: 1) Add a short demo to on-call runbook rotation, 2) schedule dashboard review with SRE in next ops triage, 3) enable feature for staging cluster by feature flag on 2026-03-03.
author_notes: I am available for pairing on the first staging enablement window. If we see excessive false positives in the first week, we will widen thresholds and deploy a config-only rollout to collect telemetry without revocations.
